drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna say they bring her up to the Eastern Gate?
outcomeNote: 'bringing up' means repeated moving to fatigue her

segments.he: הָתָם קָיְימָא! דְּמַסְּקִינַן לַהּ וּמַחֲתִינַן לַהּ כְּדֵי לְיַיגְּעָהּ. דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: בֵּית דִּין מַסִּיעִין אֶת הָעֵדִים מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם, כְּדֵי שֶׁתִּטָּרֵף דַּעְתָּן עֲלֵיהֶן וְיַחְזְרוּ בָּהֶן.
segments.en: «She is» already «standing there» in the Temple courtyard, as that is where the Sanhedrin sits. The Gemara answers: This teaches «that they» would «bring her up and» would «bring her down» repeatedly «in order to fatigue her,» with the hope that her worn-down mental state will lead to her confession. This was also done with witnesses testifying in cases of capital law, «as it is taught» in the Tosefta (Sanhedrin 9:1): «Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:» In cases of capital law, the «court brings the witnesses from» one «place to» another «place in order to confuse them so that they will retract» their testimony if they are lying.
